correctness.rationale: For every \(h\geq0\), the unique \(b\) anchors precisely \(\binom{h+2}{2}\) distinct necklaces. Counting cyclic cuts for \(a\)-before-\(b\), \(b\)-before-\(c\), and \(a\)-before-\(b\)-before-\(c\) independently yields the displayed rational matrix. Equality reduces to equal \(t+u\) and equal \((u-t-2)^2\), whose only nontrivial positive-gap coincidence is one versus three. The legal placements are precisely \(2\leq j\leq h\), each generating one doubleton. All boundary, count, and limit claims follow. A direct-rotation oracle exhaustively checks 8436 necklaces with \(h\leq35\); no finite test is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: It gives the exact zero-error observation capacity and every reconstruction ambiguity class in an infinite, mathematically motivated first nontrivial subfamily of the ternary circular Parikh equivalence problem. With a uniquely anchored \(b\), a single \(a\) is always reconstructible, whereas two \(a\) symbols admit exactly classified collisions as the \(c\)-multiplicity varies. It establishes a sharp threshold and asymptotic almost-everywhere uniqueness within the fixed composition. It neither claims a new local rewrite nor pretends to solve the general case.
